2026-09-01: Issue #162 makes frontend session work principal-owned. Auth configuration and session bootstrap start concurrently, while the protected application remains unmounted until configuration succeeds; an unavailable configuration fails closed. Session bootstrap, refresh, authenticated API responses, and protected query data are fenced to the principal that started them, so a late result cannot repopulate or replay work for a different or anonymous principal. Same-principal token refresh retains its query cache. These are frontend runtime ownership and ordering safeguards only. Backend authorization and session authority, route guards, row visibility, mutation authority, response schemas, capability fields, and permission semantics are unchanged.

Shared collections now tag successes with the normalized query identity, mask data owned by a different query during render, retain safe stale data only for the same query, fence late responses, and clear protected collection data on a confirmed 403. Shared detail presentation maps protected 403 and 404 responses to the same non-leaky unavailable outcome. The new vendorForm.mappers.ts helper only resolves the existing protected_change_requires_approval capability for Vendor form presentation. These are frontend architecture and truthful-state presentation changes only. Backend authorization remains authoritative; route guards, row visibility, mutation authority, response schemas, capability fields, fallback precedence, and frontend gate semantics are unchanged.
